# S377 — Landing: fast-forward fails after main moves during the landing

*Proposed.* A landing whose base moved after the merge-in merges it in again and retries the fast-forward once, instead of pausing; and the conflict-retry path takes the same steps as a first landing, so ork's own tracking commit is always followed by a merge-in.

**Findings:** 2026-11-16, two landings paused on "git merge --ff-only B: ... Diverging branches can't be fast-forwarded": S373 (run ork-20261116-155524-4cf4), after the orchestrator committed to main during the landing; S206 (run ork-20261116-172629-3a8b), after a merge conflict was resolved by hand and the run retried: ork's own commit d6b72802 "Tracking edits on main before landing S206" (`.slicer/log.jsonl`, one line) moved main, and the fast-forward then failed. A plain `ork retry` landed both. · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

*Proposed.* `land` (`internal/engine/land.go:62-87`) commits tracking edits in `checkMain` and loops back to `mergeBaseIn`, but in the S206 case the fast-forward still ran against a base that had moved. Each such pause needs the owner or orchestrator to run `ork retry`, though nothing needs deciding.
